notes:
Account snapshot: mid-market marketplace specializing in verticalized home & garden products. Heavy seasonality (Nov-Dec and late spring) with short spikes in search traffic. Current stack: Elasticsearch + custom TF-IDF + a CPU-hosted BERT reranker for final sort. Problems: high cost/latency on rerank, inconsistent relevance for synonyms and long-tail SKUs, scaling headaches around seasonal peaks.

Goals (from AE/SE calls):
- Reduce median search latency p95 target to <=120ms for first-page results including rerank.
- Achieve cost-per-search (end-to-end embeddings + rerank) <= $0.002 on average; willing to pay more during peaks but needs predictable unit economics.
- Index scale: ~6M SKUs (50M SKUs planned in 18 months if marketplace expansion succeeds).
- Typical rerank workflow: retrieve top 200 candidates via ANN/hybrid then rerank top 50. Seeking solutions to reduce candidate set size without hurting recall.

Tech constraints / preferences:
- Preference for embedding model families that compress well (quantized variants) and on-prem variant in future for EU customers.
- Must support SSO (SAML) and KMS integration for keys. Audit logs for compliance.
- Data residency: primary NA but planning EU region in H2; wants rollout plan.

What they tried so far:
- Elastic + approximate vectors (hot spot on CPU), BERT reranker on 8-core machines: p95 rerank latency 450-800ms, cost high.
- Piloted a GPU-based rerank in-house but lacked autoscaling and operational tooling.
- Looked at managed vector DB vendors but worried about cost at 6M+ vectors and Black Friday QPS spikes.

Quotes / snippets from discovery:
- 'We need predictable unit economics. If it spikes 5x on Black Friday, we can't triple our cloud bill.'
- 'Relevance regression is our biggest revenue risk — shoppers abandon when top results miss synonyms or color variants.'

Internal buying group:
- Head of Search (technical buyer) - Nora Patel
- VP Product (economic buyer) - Carlos Reyes
- Platform/Infra lead (security sign-off) - Mehmet Kaya
- Procurement handles Dedicated commitments

POC ask (explicit):
- Hosted POC to index 100k canonical SKUs and run simulated traffic pattern including 2hr synthetic peak at 3k QPS and baseline traffic at 350 QPS. Measure p50/p95 latency, end-to-end cost per query, and relevancy by annotated eval set (1k queries).
- Option to test Dedicated with reserved GPU pool sizing guidance if hosted meets latency but not cost targets.

Redwood value props that resonated:
- Smart routing + fallback to cheaper variants during non-peak windows.
- Prefix/KV caching to lower cost for common queries.
- Quantization guidance from Optimize to hit cost per query goals.

Suggested pitch angle from AE/SE notes:
- Start with hosted API POC with explicit cost-per-query metrics and canary plan for holiday. If results look good, convert to Dedicated with reserved capacity formula and 12-month commit.

POC timeline constraints: procurement needs a ballpark monthly committed spend by 2025-01-15 to approve Dedicated. They want the hosted POC report by 2024-12-20 to feed into procurement conversation.
